title: Multiplicity-Correction Trade-Offs in Leakage Evaluation
summary: Existing recommendations may produce excessive false positives; the open task is to improve the false-negative/false-positive trade-off through parameter choices or another correction method.

formal_statement.body: In side-channel leakage evaluation, standard multiplicity-correction recommendations can yield overall false-positive rates that are too high for a procedure that fails a device after a single rejected null hypothesis. The unresolved task is to determine whether some choice of multiplicity-correction parameters, or an alternative multiplicity-correction method, can achieve a better trade-off between the overall false-negative and false-positive rates across the relevant leakage scenarios.

scope.domain: Side-channel leakage evaluation with multiple-testing correction for cryptographic modules.
parameters: Multiplicity-correction parameters or method choice, which determine the testing procedure and its error-rate trade-off
Trace length, leakage density, number of leaks, significance level, and sample size, which affect comparative effectiveness across leakage scenarios
scope.unresolved_remainder: Whether any multiplicity-correction parameter setting or alternative method can achieve a better trade-off between overall false-negative and false-positive rates across relevant leakage scenarios.

citations.label: A Critical Analysis of ISO 17825 (‘Testing Methods for the Mitigation of Non-invasive Attack Classes Against Cryptographic Modules’)

progress.summary: The source compares several correction methods and gives scenario-specific recommendations, but explicitly leaves open whether parameter choices or another correction method can improve the error-rate trade-off.
citation_labels: Carolyn Whitnall et al., A Critical Analysis of ISO 17825 (‘Testing Methods for the Mitigation of Non-invasive Attack Classes Against Cryptographic Modules’)
